extracted.intended_audience: federal executive officials, agency leaders, agency counsel, and judicial administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations adopted by the Conference on Administrative Procedure (1953) giving procedural, organizational, and practice standards for federal agencies, the Attorney General/DOJ, and the Judicial Conference related to adjudication, rulemaking, records, and hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish Office of Administrative Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Conference recommends to the President the establishment of an Office of Administrative Procedure and that provision be made for its functions, placement, staffing, and authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation frames Office as centralized entity to study and improve agency procedures; further specifics provided in numbered sub-recommendations (functions, location in DOJ, director appointment, staff, advisory arrangements, and agency cooperation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office functions: continuous studies; uniform rules; data collection; assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: That the Office perform these functions: (a) carry on continuous studies of the adequacy of the procedures by which Federal agencies determine the rights, duties, and privileges of persons; (b) initiate cooperative effort among the agencies and their respective bars to develop and adopt as far as practicable uniform rules of practice and procedure; (c) collect and publish facts and statistics concerning the procedures of the agencies; (d) assist agencies and this Conference in the formulation and improvement of their administrative procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions emphasize monitoring, coordination among agencies and practitioners, transparency through data publication, and direct assistance in procedural reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office location and supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: That the Office be established in the Department of Justice under the supervision of the Attorney General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locates the Office within DOJ so it can coordinate agency procedure work under Attorney General oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office structure: Director and staff
rubrics_metrics.description: That the Office consist of a Director and a staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires a dedicated leadership and staff to perform continuous studies, coordination, and assistance functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director appointment term
rubrics_metrics.description: That the Director be appointed for an indefinite term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommends insulating the Director from short-term political turnover by not fixing a specific short term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director to secure advice from agencies, bar, and interested persons
rubrics_metrics.description: That the Director make appropriate arrangements for securing the advice of representatives of the agencies, the bar, and other interested persons in connection with the performance of his duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages consultative processes and stakeholder input in Office activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency cooperation duty to Office
rubrics_metrics.description: That it be the duty of each agency promptly to furnish to the Director all information on its administrative procedures which he may request and to assist him by all appropriate means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates agency responsiveness and information-sharing to enable Office studies and reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude irrelevant, immaterial, and repetitious evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: United States Courts should urge hearing officers and agencies in formal administrative proceedings to exclude irrelevant, immaterial and repetitious evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages courts to promote more efficient, focused hearings by discouraging extraneous evidence; phrased as urging rather than mandatory rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform rule for certification and filing of record in agency review
rubrics_metrics.description: Urge Courts of Appeals to adopt a uniform rule providing, in all cases where a petition to review an order of a Federal agency has been filed: (a) the time within which the certified record is to be filed; (b) that except where statute requires, the record certified may be shortened or abbreviated (i) by written stipulation of petitioner and agency, or (ii) by court order to encompass only that part of the record necessary to enable the court to pass upon issues raised; (c) that a supplemental record may be certified (i) by stipulation, or (ii) by court order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks standardization across circuits to limit record size to what is necessary for judicial review and permits supplemental records when needed; contemplates stipulation or court discretion to abbreviate records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing briefs prior to printing of full record; joint printed appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: Urge Courts of Appeals to adopt uniform rule allowing filing of a joint printed appendix containing matters of record relied on by the parties and desired by the court to be read, binding on parties when stipulated or ordered; responsibility for printing on petitioner with limitations; indexing and paging requirements; timing for briefs and appendix: petitioner's brief within 40 days after filing of transcript, respondent's brief within 30 days after petitioner's, petitioner's reply within 15 days after respondent's, joint printed appendix not later than 10 days prior to oral argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides procedural mechanics to expedite appeals from agency orders by focusing the court and parties on a jointly agreed subset of the record, with detailed timing and responsibilities; preserves other court rules when procedure not agreed to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate unnecessary delay, expense, and volume of records
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency should consider unnecessary delay, expense, and volume of records in adjudicatory and rule-making proceedings to be detrimental to the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A general principle urging agencies to proactively reduce procedural burdens and large records that impede public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive study of agency procedure to eliminate inefficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency having adjudicatory or rule-making functions should make a comprehensive and intensive study of its own procedure to discover and eliminate any unnecessary delay, expense, or volume of records which may presently occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates internal procedural review and reform to identify sources of delay, cost, and excessive record volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define status and authority of agency counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should define by rule the status of agency counsel in respects including: (a) authority of agency counsel to participate; (b) whether participation is mandatory or permissive; (c) whether, and when, agency counsel need be served with notices or papers; (d) extent to which agency counsel may take an advocate position or should confine to development of relevant materials; (e) authority to stipulate as to facts or testimony; (f) authority to settle controversies or transmit offers of settlement to the agency or its authorized officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for clear agency rules clarifying when and how agency attorneys act, and the limits of their advocacy and settlement powers to reduce confusion and improve process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define issues before hearing with particularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should require that in all proceedings the issues to be adjudicated be made initially as precise as possible so hearing officers may proceed promptly to conduct hearings on relevant and material matters only; particularity should be required in complaints, answers, applications, and petitions to intervene; in proceedings with only one interested party besides the agency, orders setting hearings should clearly specify the issues to be heard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes narrowing and clarifying issues early to focus hearings, shorten proof, and avoid irrelevant matters; applies to pleadings and hearing orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage prehearing and other conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should encourage hearing officers to call and conduct prehearing conferences and other conferences during hearings to simplify, clarify, and dispose of issues and to shorten proof on the issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotes active use of conferences to streamline proceedings and narrow contested matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a prehearing conference rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should adopt a rule authorizing the agency or its designated hearing officer, on motion or own motion, to direct parties to appear for a conference to consider: (a) simplification of issues; (b) necessity of amendments to pleadings; (c) possibility of obtaining stipulations, admissions of facts and documents; (d) limitation of number of expert witnesses; (e) such other matters as may aid disposition. The agency or hearing officer shall make an order reciting action taken, amendments allowed, agreements made, and limiting issues for hearing; such order shall control subsequent course unless modified for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides model text for a prehearing-conference rule and prescribes that conference orders govern the proceeding unless modified for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require submission of documentary evidence in advance when practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Require that, where practicable, all documentary evidence to be offered during taking of evidence be submitted to the hearing examiner and other parties sufficiently in advance to permit study and preparation of cross-examination and rebuttal; documentary evidence not submitted in advance shall not be received absent clear showing of good cause; authenticity of documents submitted in advance is deemed admitted unless written objection filed prior to hearing, subject to later challenge upon clear showing of good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to promote fairness and efficiency by providing time for opposing parties to prepare, limiting surprise documents, and streamlining authenticity objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require prepared excerpts when only portions of documents are relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: When portions only of a document are to be relied upon, the offering party shall prepare pertinent excerpts, adequately identified, supply copies with a statement indicating the purpose for which materials will be offered to the hearing examiner and other parties; only the excerpts so prepared shall be received in the record, but the whole original should be made available for examination and cross-examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits record volume by admitting only pertinent excerpts while preserving the original for verification and cross-examination; requires identification and purpose statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require agency counsel to prepare trial briefs in appropriate cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should require agency counsel to prepare in advance of hearing adequate detailed trial briefs in appropriate cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages preparation that clarifies parties' positions and evidence, aiding hearing officers and streamlining hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant broad authority to hearing officers on interlocutory matters and minimize interlocutory appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should adopt the practice that (a) broad authority be granted hearing officers to rule upon interlocutory matters which arise during hearings and interlocutory appeals from rulings should be reduced to a minimum; (b) interlocutory appeals which the agency may entertain should be disposed of promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designs process to reduce delays caused by frequent interlocutory appeals and to speed resolution when appeals are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing of large records
rubrics_metrics.description: In any formal proceeding where the record is anticipated to exceed 2,500 pages, provision should be made for a daily or current index of the record available to the hearing officer and counsel; the index should be topical (not a digest) with each topic as a heading card listing witnesses, pages of testimony, and exhibit numbers, and separate cards listing each witness and topics on which he testified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical indexing prescription to make large records navigable: topical cards, witness-topic cross-references, and exhibit mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain an adequate and detailed attorneys' manual
rubrics_metrics.description: That the agencies maintain an adequate and detailed attorneys' manual for the guidance of agency counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuals should guide agency attorneys on procedures, authority, and practice before the agency to ensure consistency and competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-service training for agency counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: That the agencies establish in-service training for agency counsel, including systematic regular instruction for newly-hired attorneys over a definite period and periodic 'refresher' courses or 'trial clinics' for experienced trial attorneys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports competency and consistent practice through required training programs for new and experienced agency lawyers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish practice manuals for practitioners before the agency
rubrics_metrics.description: That the agencies publish practice manuals of an advisory nature detailing procedural steps for all types of proceedings under each statute administered by the agency, together with customary forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to improve access and predictability for practitioners by supplying advisory practice manuals and forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperate with educational institutes and bar associations
rubrics_metrics.description: That the agencies cooperate in all feasible ways with universities and local or national bar associations undertaking to conduct practicing lawyers' institutes or courses in specialized fields of administrative law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages agencies to support continuing legal education and practical training efforts in administrative law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor conferences with the agency bar for understanding and cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: That the agencies sponsor, arrange and conduct informal meetings or conferences on a local, regional or national basis between responsible officials and members of the agency bar as an exercise of good public relations and to facilitate an atmosphere of understanding and cooperation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotes regular dialogue between agencies and practitioners to foster good relations and cooperative problem-solving.
